4

6	> to your agent: _"Read .grill-with-me/MY-ROLE.md and follow it."_ Then just answer the
7	> questions — about ten minutes. Everything below is addressed to the agent.
8

10	- src/api.ts

13	Read `grill/PROJECT.md`, any `grill/*-spec.md` files your teammates have
14	already committed, and the repo you are standing in.

16	## The grill
17	
18	Interview me relentlessly about MY LAYER ONLY — the "Backend" role —
19	until we reach a shared understanding of what I am building and what I need
20	from the other roles. Walk down each branch of the decision tree, resolving
21	dependencies between decisions one by one. For each question, provide your
22	recommended answer. Ask one question at a time — multiple questions at once
23	is bewildering.
24	
25	If a fact can be found in the repo, look it up rather than asking me. The
26	decisions are mine.

28	Prefer questions that reference something real: code that already exists in
29	this repo, or something a teammate wrote in their spec. If my answer
30	contradicts a teammate's committed spec, point at the exact line and ask
31	which of us should change.

34	- Missing ticket response
35	- Close operation boundary
36	
37	Keep a short running summary of what you have understood so far, and show it
38	to me every few questions so I can correct drift early.

41	
42	Write `grill/backend-spec.md` containing EXACTLY these five headings once
43	each, in this order, outside code fences. Individual sections may be empty;
44	a spec empty under every heading is invalid:

47	## What I own
48	## What I need from other roles
49	## Decisions made
50	## Still unclear
51	
52	Under each heading, be concrete: name endpoints as METHOD /path with request
53	and response shapes, name tables and columns with types, name files by path.
54	"An endpoint that returns items" is useless; `POST /api/rank` returning
55	`{ trails: { id: string; shadeScore: number }[] }` is what the contract
56	needs. Do not invent agreements I did not make — anything not yet agreed
57	belongs under "Still unclear".
58

60	If validation fails, correct the structure or report the missing decisions
61	before telling me to commit. Surface thin-section warnings; never invent
62	agreements just to make a section longer.

content.text:
I've read everything. Here's what I'm working from before I start asking:

- **Role** (from `.grill-with-me/MY-ROLE.md` + `.grill-with-me/member.json`): **Backend**, owning `src/api.ts`.
- **No `grill/CONTRACT.md` yet** → we're in the grilling phase, so your answers here become `grill/backend-spec.md`.
- **Repo facts I won't ask you about:** `db/schema.sql:1` has `tickets(id TEXT PRIMARY KEY, title TEXT NOT NULL, closed BOOLEAN NOT NULL DEFAULT FALSE)`. `src/api.ts:1` already declares `paths = { list: "/api/tickets", close: "/api/tickets/:id/close" }`, and both handlers are hardcoded stubs with no types and no DB access. `src/auth.ts:1` literally returns `'not yet agreed'`.
- **Teammate's committed spec** (`grill/frontend-spec.md`): reads `response.tickets` from `GET /api/tickets` (line 4), needs `POST /api/tickets/:id/close` (line 6), and "No optimistic updates. Reload the list after a successful close" (line 8).

---

**Question 1 of ~8 — the `GET /api/tickets` response shape.**

`grill/frontend-spec.md:4` pins the envelope key as `tickets`, and your stub at `src/api.ts:2` returns `{ tickets: [{ id: "t1", title: "Demo", closed: false }] }` — exactly the three columns in `db/schema.sql:1`. So the envelope is already settled by your teammate; what's open is whether the ticket object stays at those three fields.

**My recommendation:** keep it to exactly the schema's three columns —

```
GET /api/tickets → 200 { tickets: { id: string; title: string; closed: boolean }[] }
```

No `createdAt`, no pagination, no `total`. The demo only has to "List tickets" (`grill/PROJECT.md:10`), the frontend reads nothing else, and `closed` is the one field the close flow needs to reflect. Adding a timestamp would mean a schema change you'd own and the frontend doesn't consume.

Do you want those three fields only, or are you adding anything (e.g. `createdAt` for ordering)?
